question: What is the proper medical term for cervical erosion?
explanation: Cervical ectropion is the correct clinical term for cervical erosion because it describes the outward turning of the endocervical lining. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h1)

question: Why is the term 'erosion' misleading when describing this condition?

options.A: There is no actual wearing away or ulceration of the tissue
options.B: The lesion only appears on the outer surface of the vagina
options.C: The tissue is actually thickening instead of shedding
options.D: The red appearance is caused by active bacterial infection

explanation: The condition involves a displacement of cells rather than a physical breakdown or ulceration of the mucosal surface. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h1)

question: What type of tissue normally covers the ectocervix?
explanation: The ectocervix is covered by protective stratified squamous epithelium that withstands the physical environment of the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h2)

question: Where is the squamocolumnar junction located?

options.A: At the meeting point of the ectocervix and endocervix
options.B: At the superior opening leading into the uterine cavity
options.C: Along the lateral walls of the upper vaginal vault
options.D: Deep within the muscular wall of the myometrium

explanation: The squamocolumnar junction marks the dynamic border where the squamous cells of the outer cervix meet the columnar cells of the inner canal. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h2)

question: Which hormone is the primary driver of cervical ectropion development?
explanation: High levels of estrogen stimulate the growth and outward movement of the columnar cells lining the endocervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h3)

question: How do hormonal contraceptives cause cervical ectropion?

options.A: Contraceptives cause direct mechanical trauma to the outer os
options.B: Synthetic hormones mimic estrogen and stimulate columnar cell migration
options.C: Progesterone levels drop and cause rapid shedding of squamous cells
options.D: Synthetic hormones trigger an inflammatory response in the stroma

explanation: Exogenous hormones in oral contraceptives raise estrogenic activity, leading to the eversion of the endocervical epithelium. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h3)

question: What are Nabothian cysts?

options.A: Infected abscesses caused by bacterial invasion of the stroma
options.B: Malignant tumors developing from chronic cervical inflammation
options.C: Fluid-filled blisters resulting from herpes simplex virus infections
options.D: Mucus-filled retention cysts formed when squamous cells block gland ducts

explanation: Nabothian cysts develop when new metaplastic squamous epithelium covers and obstructs the openings of endocervical glands. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h4)

question: What cellular process transforms exposed columnar epithelium back into squamous epithelium?
explanation: Squamous metaplasia is the adaptive replacement process where reserve cells generate new squamous epithelium to protect the exposed cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h4)

question: What is the most common symptom reported by women with symptomatic cervical ectropion?

options.A: Foul-smelling green discharge with intense itching
options.B: Postcoital bleeding and excess mucus discharge
options.C: Severe lower abdominal cramping and high fever
options.D: Complete cessation of regular menstrual periods

explanation: The fragile, highly vascular columnar cells bleed easily upon contact and secrete excess mucus, leading to discharge and spotting. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h5)

question: Why do patients with cervical ectropion frequently experience postcoital bleeding?

options.A: The deep myometrial layers are weakened by hormonal fluctuations
options.B: Infection destroys the structural integrity of the vaginal walls
options.C: The exposed columnar epithelium has delicate capillaries that tear easily
options.D: Prolonged estrogen exposure causes ulceration of the cervix

explanation: Columnar cells on the ectocervix are fragile and lack the thick protective layers of squamous cells, making superficial capillaries vulnerable to friction. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h5)

question: Which diagnostic tool provides magnified visualization of the cervix during assessment?
explanation: A colposcope is used to examine the cervix under magnification, helping differentiate benign ectropion from dysplasia. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h6)

question: What is the primary reason for performing a Pap smear when cervical ectropion is suspected?

options.A: To definitively cure the underlying tissue displacement
options.B: To culture active bacterial growth in the canal
options.C: To rule out abnormal cell changes or malignancy
options.D: To measure circulating levels of reproductive hormones

explanation: Cytology screening is essential because visual appearance alone cannot reliably distinguish benign ectropion from pre-cancerous lesions. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h6)

question: What is the appropriate initial management for an asymptomatic patient with cervical ectropion?

options.D: Immediate surgical removal of the entire cervix

explanation: Since benign ectropion without symptoms requires no treatment, reassurance and monitoring are standard practice. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h7)

question: Why might a clinician change a patient's oral contraceptive method to manage symptomatic ectropion?

options.A: To reduce exogenous estrogen levels driving the tissue eversion
options.B: To prevent the formation of permanent malignant tumors
options.C: To accelerate the natural shedding of the myometrium
options.D: To eliminate bacterial pathogens hiding inside the uterine cavity

explanation: Switching or stopping estrogen-containing contraceptives helps decrease the hormonal stimulation causing columnar cell overgrowth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h7)

question: Which condition must always be ruled out when evaluating a patient with visible cervical redness and bleeding?
explanation: Malignancy and pre-cancerous cellular changes share visual similarities with ectropion and must be excluded through screening. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h8)

question: Why is distinguishing cervical ectropion from acute cervicitis important?

options.A: Infection makes the visual inspection of the transformation zone impossible
options.B: Ectropion prevents the transmission of sexually transmitted pathogens
options.C: Cervicitis requires specific antimicrobial treatment for infection, whereas simple ectropion does not
options.D: Cervicitis always progresses to malignant carcinoma if left untreated

explanation: Accurate diagnosis ensures that infectious causes receive appropriate antibiotic therapy rather than inappropriate surgical ablation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h8)
